name: AppFlowy
tagline: The closest open look-alike to Notion, local-first
description: Pages, databases, boards, calendars and grids in native apps that store your data on your device first. Syncing and collaboration go through AppFlowy's cloud or a self-hosted server.
licenseNote: The desktop and mobile apps are AGPL-3.0 and free for local use. The current self-hosted sync server is distributed under a commercial licence: its free tier covers one user seat and up to three guest editors, and teams pay per seat whether they self-host or use AppFlowy's cloud. The earlier AGPL server is no longer the maintained one.
backing: AppFlowy, Inc., a venture-backed startup funded by paid plans

maturity.rationale: Popular and fast-moving, but still changing shape: sync, permissions and the self-hosting licence have all shifted recently. Fine for personal use; evaluate carefully before rolling it out to a team.

selfHosting.summary: Solo use needs no server at all. Syncing between people means running AppFlowy's self-hosted server stack with Docker Compose (several services plus PostgreSQL and object storage) under its commercial licence, which is free for a single seat.

managedHosting.label: AppFlowy Cloud
managedHosting.note: Free tier for individuals; paid per seat for teams

strengths: Pages, databases, boards and calendars that feel like Notion
Works fully offline: your data lives on your device first
Imports Notion exports, including simple databases
weaknesses: Team self-hosting is not free: the sync server's free tier is a single seat
Collaboration, permissions and web publishing trail Notion and Outline
Database relations, formulas and automations need rebuilding after import
Rapid change means occasional sync bugs and breaking updates

featureNotes.realtime-collab: Needs AppFlowy Cloud or the self-hosted server
featureNotes.public-sharing: Through the sync server or cloud
